answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to verifiable useful work. Newcomers start on a shared island of reputation, completing small peer-reviewed tasks before they can transact; honest work earns trust credits that decay without continued contribution. There is no haven for throwaway accounts, since credits cannot be bought or transferred. At the zenith, influence tracks a long auditable history of helpful acts, so forging a thousand fake agents means forging a thousand honest histories, more costly than any gain.
